items.title: UK government confirms indefinite recognition of CE-marked medical devices
items.summary: The UK government has confirmed that it will continue to accept CE-marked medical devices on a long-term basis, meaning devices and in-vitro diagnostic devices (IVDs) already approved for the EU market will remain available to patients across the UK.

items.title: UK government confirms indefinite recognition of CE marked medical devices
items.summary: The UK government has confirmed that it will continue to accept CE marked medical devices on a long-term basis, meaning devices and in vitro diagnostic devices (IVDs) already approved for the EU market will remain available to patients across the UK.

items.title: Medtronic announces positive real-world results on Sphere-9 catheter and PulseSelect PFA system at APHRS 2026
items.summary: Medtronic has announced positive real-world registry results for the Affera mapping and ablation system with the Sphere-9 catheter and the PulseSelect pulsed field ablation (PFA) system.

items.title: J&J reports real-world Varipulse Pro data and 12-month Omnypulse outcomes at APHRS 2026
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (J&J) has announced new data from the VARIPURE and Omny-IRE studies presented at the 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) annual meeting (21–24 October, Busan, South Korea). Both studies were published simultaneously in Europace and Heart Rhythm, respectively.

items.title: Pascal Precision system gains US FDA approval for tricuspid valve repair
items.summary: Edwards Lifesciences has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved its Pascal Precision system for tricuspid valve repair.

items.title: German sites begin enrolment in PARADIGM trial of DurAVR TAVI valve
items.summary: Anteris Technologies has received full regulatory clearance from the German Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices (BfArM) for the DurAVR transcatheter heart valve (THV) global pivotal trial for patients with severe calcific aortic stenosis—the PARADIGM trial—patient recruitment at leading German centres and…

items.title: Non-invasive FFR tool gains US FDA clearance
items.summary: Elucid has announced US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) clearance of FFR-IQ, its software for non-invasive estimation of fractional flow reserve (FFR) from coronary CT angiography (FFR-CT).

items.title: Johnson & Johnson launches Shockwave C2 Aero Fly coronary IVL catheter in the USA
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson has announced the US launch of its Shockwave C2 Aero Fly coronary intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) catheter, designed to treat a broad range of calcified coronary artery lesions.

items.title: Haemonetics announces US FDA approval of PerQseal Elite vascular closure system
items.summary: Haemonetics has announced US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of the PerQseal Elite vascular closure system for large-bore arterial procedures.

items.title: Jupiter Endovascular reveals SPIRARE II results for Vertex thrombectomy system in intermediate-risk PE
items.summary: Jupiter Endovascular has announced the publication of full results from its SPIRARE II pivotal trial in EuroIntervention. The trial evaluated the Vertex thrombectomy system in patients with acute, intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE).

items.title: Study links statin use with lower risk of glaucoma
items.summary: People taking statins may have a lower risk of developing glaucoma or needing more intensive treatment for the condition, new research suggests. A study, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology, found statin use was associated with a 15% lower risk of developing open-angle glaucoma.

items.title: Enrolment completed in study of Freesolve resorbable magnesium scaffold
items.summary: Teleflex Incorporated has announced the successful completion of patient enrolment in the BIOMAG-LL clinical study, evaluating the safety and clinical performance of the Freesolve resorbable magnesium scaffold (RMS) in 35mm and 40mm lengths for the treatment of de novo coronary lesions up to 38mm.

items.title: SPARX trial to compare paclitaxel DCBs to stenting in complex coronary disease
items.summary: Translumina has announced the launch of the SPARX trial, an international, multicentre, randomised clinical trial comparing a first-line drug-coated balloon (DCB) strategy against contemporary drug-eluting stents (DES) in patients with complex coronary artery disease.

items.title: Endovascular Engineering receives two US FDA 510(k) clearances for PE thrombectomy devices
items.summary: Endovascular Engineering (E2) has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted 510(k) clearance for both the Hēlo thrombectomy system and Hēlo Return (blood return system).

items.title: EACTS 2026: Positive mid-term results seen with sutureless aortic valve
items.summary: Corcym has announced positive mid-term data from a sub-analysis of its Perceval Plus sutureless aortic heart valve as part of the MANTRA clinical trial. The data featured in an oral presentation today at the annual meeting of the European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS, 7–10 October, Barcelona, Spain).

items.title: AngioDynamics appoints Eric Honroth as president and chief executive officer
items.summary: AngioDynamics has announced the appointment of Eric Honroth as president and chief executive officer and a member of the board of directors, effective 2 November 2026. Honroth will succeed Jim Clemmer, who will depart the board on the same date but will remain in a consulting capacity.

items.title: Lessons from two decades of carotid stent use: Implications for today’s practice
items.summary: This advertorial, sponsored by Abbott, is only intended for readers in the USA. Peter Faries (Mount Sinai Health System, New York, USA) recounts his extensive clinical experience in the field of carotid stenting, highlighting design developments, procedural advances, and pivotal data.

items.title: NHS England — Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) for Atrial Fibrillation (C477380)
items.summary: Preliminary market consultation to inform NHS Commercial Strategy for Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) for Atrial Fibrillation Responses by 30/10/2026 10:00.

items.title: US FDA 510(k) — Khelix Magnetic Sensor Electrophysiology Catheter (SS1-*-*-MAG)
Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) for Atrial Fibrillation
items.summary: NHS England. Preliminary market consultation to inform the NHS commercial strategy for Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) for Atrial Fibrillation. Please note all stated financial values in relation to this notice are nominal, as the financial envelope is yet to be defined.

items.title: Statins may protect against common cause of blindness
items.summary: Taking statins could provide protection against one of the commonest causes of blindness in old age, according to US research published this week.

items.title: Pregnancy complications ‘linked’ to later cardiovascular and kidney disease
items.summary: Pregnancy complications including preterm birth and miscarriage may indicate an increased risk of future cardiovascular, metabolic and kidney disorders, according to a new UK study.

items.title: Surmodics adds ultra-thin polymer surface modification technology to its haemocompatible portfolio
items.summary: Surmodics has announced that it has acquired the business of Alta Biomed, a medical device coating and testing services company specialising in surface technologies for vascular and other medical devices.

items.title: HeartBeam receives US FDA Breakthrough Device designation for heart attack assessment
items.summary: HeartBeam has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Breakthrough Device designation for the HeartBeam system as a tool for assessing potential heart attacks at home.

items.title: STORM-PE subset analysis demonstrates correlation between clinical assessments and real-world functional recovery
items.summary: Penumbra has announced results from a subset analysis of the STORM-PE randomised controlled trial (RCT), which, according to the company, is the first trial to demonstrate a significant correlation between real-world, daily step-based activity as captured on a consumer wearable device and patient performance in the…

items.title: Cambridge Heartwear wins £184m NHS Supply Chain tender for HeartSense ECG wearable
items.summary: NHS Supply Chain has awarded Cambridge Science Park spinout Cambridge Heartwear a £184m tender to supply its HeartSense device, a wirelessly charged, reusable multi-channel ECG wearable, across primary and secondary care.

items.title: CVD benefits of semaglutide not fully explained by weight loss
items.summary: The cardiovascular benefits of the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide cannot be fully explained by weight loss or improvements in other known risk factors, according to a new analysis of a major clinical trial.

items.title: Twenty-fifth patient treated with Recross PFO sealing system as part of PROTEA-PFO study
items.summary: Recross Cardio has announced the treatment of the 25th subject in the PROTEA-PFO clinical programme evaluating the Recross PFO sealing system.

items.title: BACKBEAT trial of AVIM therapy exceeds enrolment goal
items.summary: Orchestra BioMed has announced that it has surpassed full enrolment in the BACKBEAT global pivotal trial, exceeding its previously announced target of 316 randomised patients.

items.title: BACKBEAT trial of AVIM therapy exceeds enrolment goal
items.summary: Orchestra BioMed has announced that it has surpassed full enrolment in the BACKBEAT global pivotal trial, exceeding its previously announced target of 316 randomised patients.

items.title: First US commercial cases completed with Emboliner embolic protection system
items.summary: Emboline has announced the first commercial use of its Emboliner embolic protection system.

items.title: SCAD ALIGN trial secures US funding to investigate optimal treatment for spontaneous coronary dissection
items.summary: The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (New York, USA) has received a US$2 million grant from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), part of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), to study which therapy is optimal for treating spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD).

items.title: AMA assigns new CPT codes for renal denervation
items.summary: The American Medical Association (AMA) has approved two new category I current procedural terminology (CPT) codes describing renal denervation.

items.title: Size adjustable pulmonary valve gains US FDA approval
items.summary: Edwards Lifesciences has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Autus size-adjustable valve, a surgical pulmonary valve designed specifically for paediatric patients with congenital heart disease who require pulmonary valve replacement.

items.title: Weekly isometric exercise training benefits for blood pressure
items.summary: A weekly session of isometric exercise training may maintain lower blood pressure, but less frequent training might be a pragmatic option for people with limited time, according to UK researchers.

items.title: No net benefit for no-touch graft harvesting technique at seven years
items.summary: Seven-year follow-up data from the SWEDEGRAFT trial, testing the ‘no-touch’ technique for graft harvesting for coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, do not establish a net clinical benefit for the routine use of the technique, investigators say.

items.title: Medtronic announces regulatory milestones for newest cardiac mapping and ablation software
items.summary: Medtronic today announced regulatory milestones for software used with two cardiac ablation platforms, including US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance and a CE mark for the latest Affera Prism-2 mapping software.

items.title: Hybrid endoscopic imaging system gets expanded indication for cardiac surgery procedures
items.summary: Karl Storz has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared expanded indications for the TIPCAM1 Rubina video endoscope for use in selected cardiac surgical procedures.

items.title: Medtech incubator backs novel transcatheter implant for functional mitral regurgitation
items.summary: Mitria Medical, an early-stage, structural heart company developing a next-generation transcatheter solution for mitral valve repair, has announced a partnership with T45 Labs, a Silicon Valley medtech incubator focused on minimally invasive cardiovascular technologies.

items.title: FastWave shares interim results for Sola L-IVL system
items.summary: FastWave Medical has announced interim results from the first-in-human (FIH) feasibility study of its Sola laser intravascular lithotripsy (L-IVL) system for treating calcified coronary artery disease. Thirty patients were treated at two clinical sites.

items.title: AI, ablation innovation and multidisciplinary education to take centre stage at 2026 Heart Rhythm Congress
items.summary: The 2026 Heart Rhythm Congress (HRC; 11–13 October, Birmingham, UK) is set to bring the international heart rhythm community—clinicians, researchers, allied health professionals, patients and industry—together once again, focusing on artificial intelligence (AI), the future of cardiac ablation, and more.

items.title: Innovative tricuspid TEER system wins TCT Plus Middle East Shark Tank competition
items.summary: Startric, the developer of a next-generation transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) system for the treatment of tricuspid heart valve disease, has been named as the winner of the Shark Tank cardiovascular innovation competition at the 2026 TCT Plus Middle East conference (17–19 September, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia).

items.title: AI software for detecting undiagnosed MR gains US FDA approval
items.summary: Tempus AI has received 510(k) clearance from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for Tempus ECG-MR, an AI product that analyses standard 12-lead resting electrocardiograms (ECGs) to detect signs associated with undiagnosed moderate or severe mitral regurgitation (MR).

items.title: Delays in receiving TAVI linked to higher risk of heart failure hospitalisation or mortality
items.summary: Prolonged delays in receiving transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) after a diagnosis of severe aortic stenosis (AS) may be associated with a higher risk of hospitalisation for heart failure or all-cause mortality, a real-world, single-centre study from Japan has found.

items.summary: Journal of Paramedic Practice, Volume 18, Issue 10, Page 403-403, October 2026.…

items.title: StopAfib.org announces recipient of 2026 Eric N Prystowsky Advocate for Patients Award
items.summary: At its recent annual patient conference (7–9 August, Dallas, USA), StopAfib.org bestowed its prestigious Eric N Prystowsky Advocate for Patients Award on Jonathan Piccini (Duke University, Durham, USA) to recognise his “outstanding commitment” to atrial fibrillation (AF) patients and their families.
